title: Scalar extension preserves finite presentations of internal module objects
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme and give $\mathcal C=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ its sheaf tensor product [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $R,S$ be commutative ring objects of $\mathcal C$ [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], and let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a ring-object morphism. For an $R$-module object $M$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], suppose $M$ is finitely presented [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module], meaning that $M\cong\operatorname{coker}(R^m\to R^n)$ for finite $m,n$. Then $\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}(M)=S\otimes_R M$ [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] is finitely presented as an $S$-module object. No flatness hypothesis is required.

source.place: second sentence, tensoring the local finite presentation; internal finite-free presentation argument expanded using def-sfb-finitely-presented-module

proof.text: Use the small pro-étale site in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], on its chosen $\mathcal V$-small skeleton. The example $\mathcal A=\Ab$ in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] satisfies the Grothendieck-abelian coefficient hypotheses of [lem-sfb-grothendieck-sheafification], whose final assertion makes $\mathcal C$ abelian. The sheaf tensor is symmetric monoidal and preserves colimits in each variable by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. In particular tensoring preserves the zero object and finite coproducts, hence is additive: it preserves the canonical injections and projections and thus the diagonal/codiagonal formula for addition of morphisms. Apply [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] to $R$ and to $S$; both tensor-left functors preserve finite colimits. Consequently $\operatorname{Mod}_R(\mathcal C)$ and $\operatorname{Mod}_S(\mathcal C)$ are abelian. Their finite biproducts and cokernels exist by [def-sp-abelian]. Ambient coequalizers also exist, as cokernels of differences of parallel arrows. Thus the braidedness, coequalizer and tensor-colimit-preservation hypotheses for scalar extension and for the mixed-bimodule right unitor below all hold.

source.place: Sheaf tensor, examples and clauses 1–2; abelian module-category hypotheses of lem-sfb-modobj-abelian.md

proof.text: By [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module], choose finite $m,n$, an $R$-linear map $f:R^m\to R^n$, its cokernel $q:R^n\to Q$, and an $R$-module isomorphism $M\cong Q$. The powers here are finite biproducts of the regular module, and rank zero means the zero object. Write $F=\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi$.

source.place: Second sentence: choose the finite-free presentation before tensoring

proof.text: The construction [def-sfb-modobj-extension] makes $P=S$ an $S$-$R$-bimodule, with left action $\mu_S$ and right action $\rho_P=\mu_S\circ(S\otimes\varphi)$. For the regular $R$-module its displayed coequalizer is exactly $P\otimes_R R$: the two maps are $\rho_P\otimes R$ and $(S\otimes\mu_R)\circ\alpha_{S,R,R}$, and the left $S$-action is through the first factor in both constructions. Apply [lem-sfb-mixed-bimodule-right-unitor] to this $P$, then forget its right $R$-action. It gives an $S$-linear isomorphism $e_1:F(R)\xrightarrow{\sim}S$. The forward map is induced by $\rho_P$ and its inverse inserts the unit of $R$ before the coequalizer map. This uses no equality $R=S$ and no flatness.

source.place: Second sentence, finite-free terms after tensoring; balanced-tensor right-unit identification

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-modobj-extension-right-exact], $F$ preserves finite colimits. In particular it takes the initial object $0$ to an initial object; since the target is abelian, this gives $F(0)\cong0$. A zero morphism factors through $0$, so its image under $F$ factors through a zero object and is zero. A finite biproduct $R^k$ is also the coproduct of $k$ copies of $R$. Preservation of this finite coproduct and the isomorphism $e_1$ from step 3 give $e_k:F(R^k)\xrightarrow{\sim}S^k$: its restriction to the $i$th coproduct inclusion is the $i$th inclusion of $S$ composed with $e_1$. The coproduct universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives the inverse using $e_1^{-1}$, and both composites are identities because they are identities on every inclusion. For $k=0$ this is the initial-object comparison. Thus these are isomorphisms in the module category for all finite ranks, including $m,n$.

source.place: Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact (1), applied to finite discrete and empty diagrams; Tag 002F, definition-colimit, for the comparison maps

proof.text: A cokernel of $f$ is precisely a coequalizer of $(f,0)$: its coequalizing equation is $qf=0$, and its factorization property is the cokernel property written in [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. This is a finite colimit, so [lem-sfb-modobj-extension-right-exact] makes $F(q):F(R^n)\to F(Q)$ a cokernel of $F(f)$, since $F(0)=0$ on morphisms by step 4. Set $g=e_n\circ F(f)\circ e_m^{-1}:S^m\to S^n$ and $p=F(q)\circ e_n^{-1}:S^n\to F(Q)$. Then $pg=0$. If $h:S^n\to N$ satisfies $hg=0$, the identity $g e_m=e_n F(f)$ implies $(h e_n)F(f)=0$. There is a unique $u:F(Q)\to N$ with $uF(q)=h e_n$, hence $up=h$. Conversely $up=h$ implies $uF(q)=h e_n$, so uniqueness is unchanged. Thus $F(Q)$ is a cokernel of $g$. The uniqueness clause for colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $F(Q)\cong\operatorname{coker}(g)$.

source.place: Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact (1), applied to the finite parallel-pair diagram; Tag 002F, definition-colimit, uniqueness

proof.text: Apply the functor $F$ to the chosen isomorphism $M\cong Q$; the images of its two inverse maps are again inverse by the functor laws. Composing with step 5 gives $F(M)\cong\operatorname{coker}(g)$ for an $S$-linear $g:S^m\to S^n$. This is finite presentation over $S$ by [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. Only finite-colimit preservation was used; injectivity of a presentation map and flatness are unnecessary.

source.place: Second sentence, conclusion that tensoring gives a finite presentation (right exactness)

There are no new nodes. The statement is unchanged and true. It is the second sentence of main-20261015 lem-sfb-extend-subfield-constructible.proof.md (tensoring a local finite presentation, by right exactness), and it fits the parent's uses in steps 2 and 3 (commutative ring objects E_U, F_U and the coefficient isomorphisms). Small cases tested: m=0, n=0, f=0, S=0, and the non-flat Z→Z/2 with M=Z/2, which gives the zero map on Z/2 with cokernel Z/2. Step 1: the V-small pro-étale skeleton and Ab at universe V meet the hypotheses of lem-sfb-grothendieck-sheafification, so Sh is abelian. Additivity of the tensor follows from its preserving colimits. lem-sfb-modobj-abelian then applies to R and to S, which discharges the hypotheses of def-sfb-modobj-extension and of the mixed unitor. Step 3: at M=R the two coequalizer arrows of def-sfb-modobj-extension are exactly P⊗_R R in lem-sfb-mixed-bimodule-right-unitor with P=S and ρ=μ_S(S⊗φ). That node is the Mathlib leaf Bimod.rightUnitorBimod (Bimod.lean:764), which takes distinct monoids X and Y, so this is correct. Steps 4 and 5: lem-sfb-modobj-extension-right-exact preserves the initial object (so F sends zero morphisms to zero), finite coproducts and the coequalizer of (f,0). The conjugation by e_m and e_n is written out with existence and uniqueness. Steps 2 and 6 are genuinely elementary. No flatness, left exactness or SGA is used, and nothing is circular. I accept the three declared tool uses (grothendieck-sheafification, modobj-abelian, extension-right-exact) as generic black boxes.
